answer: Bond each output, not each identity: each output enters the cedar archive only after locking a 25-credit bond sealed by a cipher receipt, frozen until acceptance; a river ledger lists bonds for audit. Rejected outputs burn their bonds; one receipt covers one output, so no recycling. Splitting buys nothing: 1,000 fakes filing 10 outputs lock 250,000 credits; the k-th concurrent output from one identity costs 25+5(k-1) credits. A rented-output ring fails: each rented output needs its own bond; rejection burns it. An honest agent bonds only its own outputs and recovers each.
